title: Tenancy surge moderator and adaptive warmth creditor for fair burst allocation
author: Nikhil Rao
release_notes: Introduces a tenancy-aware surge moderation layer and an adaptive warmth-credit allocator to reduce noisy neighbor burst impact and improve SLA stability for Dedicated fleets. Backwards-compatible operator flags for gradual rollout.
commits: a1c9d2e - introduce tenancy surge moderator core loop and tests
b3f4c77 - add adaptive warmth creditor and amortized credit ledger
c8d5fae - telemetry: expose tenant_surge_score and warmth_credit metrics
d12b9ab - integration: e2e scenario for surge across mixed-tenancy pools
description:
Context and motivation: In multi-tenant Dedicated fleets we observe repeated microbursts from a small set of tenants causing downstream latency spikes for colocated tenants and triggering conservative autoscaler reactions. Existing reservation and warm-pool logic is agnostic to short-term surge composition which leads to oscillation and worst-case SLA violations for mid-tier customers. This PR introduces a tenancy-aware Surge Moderator and an Adaptive Warmth Creditor to smooth transient microbursts without changing long-term commitments.

Summary of changes: 1) Surge Moderator: a short-running control loop that computes a tenant_surge_score using request rate, recent latency tail, and KV-cache pressure. The moderator applies a proportional governor that temporarily reduces burst headroom for tenants whose surge_score exceeds a tunable threshold, while recording credits. 2) Adaptive Warmth Creditor: when tenants underutilize reserved capacity, creditor accumulates warmth_credit and can repay moderated tenants during sustained surges. Credits decay with a configurable half-life to prevent unbounded accumulation. 3) Telemetry: new metrics tenant_surge_score, warmth_credit_balance, moderated_headroom, and moderation_events counter; added Prometheus labels for tenant_id, pool_id, and priority_class. 4) Operator flags and Helm values to opt-in and tune thresholds for canary rollout. 5) Integration tests that simulate mixed-tenancy bursts and assert reduced cross-tenant latency tail and fewer aggressive autoscaler triggers.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-2190)
- [x] Unit tests for moderator and creditor logic (pkg/autoscaler/*_test.go)
- [x] Integration test (tests/integration/tenancy_surge_test.go)
- [x] Metrics emitted and documented (pkg/telemetry/*)
- [x] Helm values and operator flagging for staged rollout
- [x] Backwards-compatible defaults (feature off by default)

High level commits: a1c9d2e (core loop + tests), b3f4c77 (creditor ledger), c8d5fae (metrics plumbing), d12b9ab (integration harness).

CI and validation: Initial CI runs showed a flaky integration failure in tenancy_surge_test on the second test vector (timeout). Root cause: the test used an unrealistic request schedule; I added jitter and deterministic time advancing in the harness. Rerun passing: all unit and integration suites passed on the final run. Lint/format and go vet were clean.

Review conversation (summary):
- Erin Delgado: "Can we bound how many credits a single tenant can hoard?"
  - Nikhil: "Yes — creditor caps per-tenant balance to 2x reserved headroom; added cap and tests."
- Marco Ivankov: "The moderation signal looks correlated with KV cache pressure; can we avoid thrashing?"
  - Nikhil: "Added exponential smoothing in surge_score and a 30s minimum moderation window to avoid flip-flop (documented in README)."
- Sana Patel: "Please ensure operator flags default to off and we can enable per-pool tone."
  - Nikhil: "Flags default to false; Helm chart has per-pool overrides. Added docs page for ops runbook."
- QA (internal): "Observed 12% reduction in 95th pct latency for victim tenants across the simulated traffic matrix."

Migration and rollout plan: Feature gate off by default. Recommend canary on a single low-risk Dedicated pool for 72 hours with metrics and alerting: moderation_events > 0 and warmth_credit_balance trending. If satisfactory, enable for more pools in stages. Operator flags: --enable-tenancy-moderator, --moderation-threshold, --credit-decay-secs, --max-credit-multiplier.

Merge outcome: squash-merged to main after approvals from Erin and Marco. Follow-up work tracked in ENG-2207 (auto-tuning moderation thresholds) and a separate card for long-term credit accounting across TTLs.
